subject: Post-call: deployment decision inputs (TPS, concurrency, GPU preference)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
To: Lena Morales <lena@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment decision inputs (TPS, concurrency, GPU preference)

Hi Lena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the minimal inputs we need to size a Dedicated pool vs recommend Hosted or Private: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary workload: real-time recommendations + short summarization of events.
- Latency target: p95 <= 220ms for single-turn responses (some background batch jobs allowed up to 1s).
- Regulatory note: want VPC option but prefer Redwood-hosted Dedicated if possible.

What we need from you to finalize a preliminary sizing: (one-line answers are perfect)
1) Peak sustained TPS (tokens per second) or requests per second during peak windows.
2) Typical concurrency per customer/session (how many simultaneous request streams do you expect?).
3) Average token breakdown: prompt tokens vs response tokens (or tokens per request average).
4) Model preference or constraints (e.g., need T5-like model, plan to use an LLM with ~70B params, or open to quantized variants).
5) Any on-prem/VPC-only constraints that would rule out Hosted/Dedicated.
6) Target monthly token volume (ballpark ok for cost comparisons).

Attachments: I attached a one-page template (acme_token_mix_estimate.xlsx) — please fill the top section and send back. That'll let our infra team sketch GPU type (A100/H100/L4), pool size, and expected latency/cost.

Next steps I propose:
- You send the quick numbers above by EOD Wednesday (Sep 2).
- If numbers are unclear, we set a 30-min technical sizing call with Marissa (our Solutions Eng lead) and Aditya (inference engineer).

Thanks — happy to coordinate time.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0193
From: Lena Morales <lena@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment decision inputs (TPS, concurrency, GPU preference)

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the clear recap. Attached a rough fill of your template (acme_token_mix_estimate.xlsx). Quick answers inline below: 

1) Peak sustained: ~1.5K requests/minute for the global peak, which is ~25 RPS sustained for that window. For token-level, peak tokens/s ~1,600 tokens/s including responses.
2) Concurrency: expectation is 40 concurrent streams during peak for our busiest tenant.
3) Token breakdown: average prompt ~120 tokens; average response ~220 tokens (so ~340 tokens/request).
4) Model preference: we want to evaluate a 70B open model family first; willing to test quantized int8/int4 variants to reduce cost. Latency is priority over ultra-high fidelity.
5) On-prem: not required today; VPC+dedicated capacity is preferred for data isolation and egress controls.
6) Monthly tokens: estimate 2.5B prompts + 4.5B responses (~7B tokens/mo) during initial rollout.

Notes: procurement will want an expected monthly cost band for Hosted vs Dedicated for procurement review. Also happy to set a technical call.

Best,
Lena Morales
Director of Product | Acme Analytics
lena@acmeanalytics.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
To: Lena Morales <lena@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment decision inputs (TPS, concurrency, GPU preference)

Lena — perfect, thanks for the fast answers and the sheet. That's enough for a first-pass. Looping in Marissa and Aditya to validate sizing assumptions and propose a config.

Initial reading (high-level):
- With ~1,600 tokens/s peak and avg 340 tokens/request, we're looking at sustained peak concurrency consistent with your 25 RPS and 40 logical streams.
- For a 70B family and p95 latency target ~220ms, likely starting points:
  * H100 80GB x2–3 for the hot pool (best p95 but higher cost), or
  * A100 80GB x3–4 for balanced cost/latency, or
  * L4 clusters for aggressive quantized variants if model quality allows.

Marissa / Aditya — can you confirm the rough GPU count estimate and whether we should recommend a dedicated reserved pool vs Hosted with fallback? Points to consider:
- Expected token mix and whether we can leverage prefix caching (how much prompt reuse?)
- KV cache hit rate expectations — if high, effective throughput increases and GPU count can drop
- Can we meet p95 <=220ms with the 70B quantized model on A100 vs H100 at the numbers Lena provided?

Lena / Tom — can you share an example prompt set or confirm prompt reuse percentage? Also, any hard SLA requirements (uptime/SLOs) procurement will need called out for Dedicated contracts?

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa to propose 2 sizing options (cost-optimized and latency-optimized) by Thu Sep 3.
- 45-min technical sizing call to review numbers this week if possible — Marissa, Aditya let us know availability.

Thanks — I'll prepare a short comparison doc (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) for procurement.

Sean
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
Cc: Lena Morales <lena@acmeanalytics.com>, Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment decision inputs (TPS, concurrency, GPU preference)

Thanks Sean — digging in. Quick engineering check and clarifying questions for sizing: 

Assumptions I'll validate:
- Model: 70B quantized int8 candidate (we'll also test int4 if quality acceptable).
- Peak token rate: 1,600 tokens/s sustained for short bursts (we should know burst duration).
- Concurrency: 40 active streams; expected KV cache hit ~25% (please confirm).
- Latency target: p95 <= 220ms (hard requirement?).

Questions for Acme (Lena):
1) Burst profile: is the 25 RPS sustained for >10 minutes, or is it short spikes (~1–2 minutes)?
2) Do you expect any heavy context windows ( >2k tokens) for certain workflows?
3) Is prefix/prompt reuse across sessions high (e.g., same system prompt + small user edits)?

Preliminary sizing note (ballpark):
- Latency-optimized: H100 80GB pool of 3 instances with autoscale for brief spikes. This targets p95 ~180–220ms for 70B int8 depending on KV cache hit.
- Cost-optimized: A100 80GB pool of 4 instances, target p95 ~230–300ms (may need to adjust prompt truncation to hit 220ms).

I'll run a quick microbench this week against a sample prompt set if Lena can share a short deck or a few representative prompts. That will let us validate p95 numbers and quantify how much caching helps.

Tom / Lena — when is a good time for a 45-min call? My calendar is open Thu 9/3 10–11am PT or Fri 9/4 8–11am PT.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
From: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
Cc: Lena Morales <lena@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment decision inputs (TPS, concurrency, GPU preference)

Marissa — thanks for the options. Quick answers: 
- Burst profile: peaks of ~20–30 minutes during business hours for new feature releases, plus short 1–5 minute spikes. Plan for conservative autoscaling.
- Context windows: mostly short (<1k tokens) but some ad-hoc flows hit ~2.5k tokens.
- Prompt reuse: high for system prompts and templates; estimate prefix reuse ~45%.

We can do Thu 9/3 10:00am PT for the 45-min technical call. I'll upload a small sample prompt set and a short SLO doc (prod_slo_requirements.pdf) to the Drive link you shared.

Thanks — Tom
VP Engineering | Acme Analytics
